head: e2f543a617bb8caa362f56448e5f170749989c9a
title: Avoid copying unused hidden layers in WeightedLayerPooling
body:
## Change

Select the requested hidden layers before stacking them in WeightedLayerPooling. Stacking every encoder layer first copies unused activations and retains that larger backing storage for backward even though the reduction only reads the selected suffix.

The weighted multiply and reduction keep their existing order. Earlier encoder parameters still receive gradients through the selected hidden states. This is independent of #4303, which registers custom weight tensors.

## Validation

[Exact-base CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43914106445) compares base `9ac7fdb4` and candidate `e2f543a6` on PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**:

- Baseline: **1 failed, 27 passed**; the storage regression exposes retention of all 13 hidden-state copies.
- Candidate plus adjacent pooling tests: **275 passed, 156 skipped** in each environment. Skips are the existing optional-backend and unavailable CUDA cases.
- Independent weighted-mean and connected encoder tests compare outputs, input gradients, trainable weights and all encoder parameter gradients. FP16/BF16 tests preserve the original reduction and rounding exactly; list/tuple inputs, negative layer offsets and missing hidden states are covered.
- All pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The [reproducible benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/a00e2cbbb099b9d5871dfc2654888271771f581d/.validation/st-weighted-layer-benchmark.py) measures full pooling forward/backward with batch 8, 256 tokens, 768 dimensions, float32, one CPU thread, two warmups and seven timed runs. Outputs and selected-layer/weight gradients are bit-identical to baseline.

| PyTorch 2.14.1 case | Before median | After median | Ratio | Unique saved tensor storage |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 13 hidden states, start 4 | 199.65 ms | 156.49 ms | 1.28× | 84.0 → 60.0 MiB |
| 25 hidden states, start 21 | 190.48 ms | 46.70 ms | 4.08× | 156.0 → 30.0 MiB |

PyTorch 2.6.0 measured 2.07× and 4.86× on the same cases. Storage counts unique tensors retained by autograd, not peak process memory. Encoder execution is outside these component measurements; GPU performance was not measured.
